title: Stored photometry for a past session is invisible: the light curve is filtered by the CURRENT global target selection, so reviewing any other night shows "has no data yet"
what_happened: Analytics > Science with 'Night D - V-Test' selected (120 frames, 480 photometry_measurements rows of which 120 are role='target', object_id='V-TEST', differential_magnitude sweeping -0.30..+0.30) renders 'Differential Photometry has no data yet', Period Analysis 'Need at least 10 photometry points (0 available)', no 'Export to AAVSO' button, and the Science guide ladder stuck on rung 2 'Track a star'.
expected: Reviewing a stored session should plot the photometry that session actually recorded. The DB holds a complete 120-point light curve for it.
repro: Proved by A/B in the running app. sessionLightCurveProvider filters photometry rows to objectId == activePhotometryTargetObjectIdProvider, which is `selection?.target?.objectId ?? 'target_primary'` - a single GLOBAL live selection, not a per-session lookup. I inserted 20 rows into session 5 identical in every way except object_id='target_primary'; after restart the Differential Photometry chart for Night E drew them (dMag axis -0.40..0.40, x 0s..1h35m) and the AAVSO export button appeared, while Night D's 120 real points stayed invisible.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/ra2-05.png (Night D: ladder stalled at 'Track a star', 'Pick a target'); tree for Night D shows 'Differential Photometry has no data yet' + 'Need at least 10 photometry points (0 available)'; tree for Night E after the target_primary insert shows a drawn 'Differential Photometry' chart with dMag ticks and 'Export to AAVSO'. sqlite: select object_id,role,count(*) from photometry_measurements group by 1,2 -> V-TEST|target|120 for session 4.
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/science_provider/session_products.dart:299-325 (sessionLightCurveProvider) and photometry_selection.dart:203-206 (activePhotometryTargetObjectIdProvider); write side uses selection.target!.objectId at services/science/science_processing_service/private_helpers.dart:169+
proposed_fix: For review mode, derive the object list from the session's own rows (select distinct object_id where role='target' and session_id=?) and offer a picker defaulting to the one with the most points; only fall back to the live selection for the session currently being captured.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced by driving the A/B myself. With 'Night D - V-Test' selected the Science tab renders 'Differential Photometry has no data yet' and 'Need at least 10 photometry points (0 available)', no Export to AAVSO, ladder stuck on rung 2 'Track a star' - while sqlite shows session 4 holds 480 photometry_measurements rows, 120 of them role='target' object_id='V-TEST' with a non-null differential_magnitude on every one. Changing only the session picker to 'Night E - M13' immediately draws a Differential Photometry chart with a dMag axis, surfaces 'Export to AAVSO', and Period Analysis reports 'analyze 80 data points' - because session 5's rows carry object_id='target_primary'. That object_id is the sole difference. I closed the loop from persisted state rather than inference: app_settings holds science.photometry.target_anchor = '' (empty), so photometry_selection.dart:205 `selection?.target?.objectId ?? 'target_primary'` yields the literal 'target_primary' and session_products.dart:313 filters `row.objectId == args.$2`. Both cited locations are exact (provider begins :299, filter :313; activePhotometryTargetObjectIdProvider :203-205). A stored night's light curve is unreachable and un-exportable unless the live selection happens to name the same object.

title: Science guide ladder is stuck on rung 1 and tells the user to "turn on live photometry" while the same page plots an 80-point light curve, a period and an Export to AAVSO button
what_happened: Analytics > Science with Night E - M13 selected. The Science guide highlights rung 1 'Measure your sky' with the action 'Run calibration'. Opening rung 3 'Build a light curve' shows a padlock and 'Turn on live photometry and track a star to start collecting points.' Opening rung 5 'Contribute it' shows 'Find a period - or build out the curve - before exporting.' On the SAME scroll of the SAME page: Differential Photometry draws 80 points, Period Analysis reports 'Lomb-Scargle Best Period 21.2 min' and 'BLS Best Period 21.8 min', and an enabled 'Export to AAVSO' button sits under the chart.
expected: The ladder is the app's own statement of how far the user has got. It must be derived from the same data the cards below it are rendering. Telling a user to start collecting points when 80 points are on screen, and to find a period when one is displayed, makes the guide untrustworthy and hides the export the user is being told to work toward.
repro: Seed 80 photometry_measurements rows whose object_id matches the active photometry target for the selected session; open Analytics > Science; press Run Period Search; then click ladder rungs 3 and 5.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/ra3-07-rung3.png (rung 3 sheet: padlock + 'Turn on live photometry and track a star to start collecting points'); tree for rung 5: 'Find a period - or build out the curve - before exporting.'; /tmp/ns-audit/shots/ra3-01.png (same page: LS 21.2 min / BLS 21.8 min); tree of the same page lists 'button: Export to AAVSO'.
location_wrong: The rung-unlock predicates are indeed in science_ladder_model.dart (evaluateLadder, :95-139), but the two quoted locked-reason strings are NOT in science_rung_sheet.dart - they are in science_onboarding/science_ladder_card.dart:181 and :184. A fixer sent to science_rung_sheet.dart would find neither string.
proposed_fix: Compute rung state from the stored session products (photometry point count, period-analysis result, calibration rows) rather than from the live in-process pipeline flags, which are empty whenever the tab is used to review a past session - i.e. almost always.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with 80 photometry measurements on the selected session: the Science guide highlights rung 1 'Measure your sky' with CTA 'Run calibration'; rung 3 'Build a light curve' shows 'Turn on live photometry and track a star to start collecting points.'; rung 5 'Contribute it' shows 'Find a period - or build out the curve - before exporting.' On the same scroll, Differential Photometry plots 80 points, an enabled 'Export to AAVSO' button sits under it, and Period Analysis returns a result. The partial fix already applied to evaluateLadder (:100, track unlocks on lightCurvePoints > 0) is dead here because measure != done forces track=locked, cascading curve/period/contribute to locked.

title: Exported MPC 80-column report puts the CCD observation-type code in column 14 instead of column 15, so every record is malformed
what_happened:
Analytics > Science > ANOMALIES > MPC Report Export > Select All > Export to File produced /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/mpc_report_2026-08-02T15-14-07-815531Z.txt with two 80-character records:
     NS0001  C 2026 08 01.12847 16 41 41.64 +36 27 40.7           17.4V      W88
Column-by-column that is: 1-5 blank, 6-12 'NS0001 ', 13 ' ', 14 'C', 15 ' ', 16-32 date, 33-44 RA, 45-56 Dec, 57-65 blank, 66-70 ' 17.4', 71 'V', 72-77 blank, 78-80 'W88'. The MPC's 80-column format defines column 14 as Note 1 and column 15 as Note 2, and it is Note 2 that carries the observation type ('C' = CCD). Skotiq writes 'C' into Note 1 and leaves Note 2 blank.
expected: Column 15 = 'C', column 14 blank. As exported, every observation the user submits reaches the MPC with no observation type and a non-standard Note 1 - the exact thing the MPC's submission checker rejects.
repro: Set Settings > Science > MPC observatory code (I set app_settings 'science.mpc.observatory_code' = 'W88'). Analytics > Science > MPC Report Export > Select All > Export to File. Read columns 14 and 15 of the output.
evidence: /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/mpc_report_2026-08-02T15-14-07-815531Z.txt; column extraction printed above; source confirms it is deliberate: mpc_export_service.dart:180-185 `// Column 14: Note 1 - C = CCD observation` `const note1 = 'C';` `// Column 15: Note 2 - blank` `const note2 = ' ';`
proposed_fix: Swap them: `const note1 = ' '; const note2 = 'C';` and fix the two comments. Add a unit test asserting line[14] == 'C' (0-indexed) for a CCD observation.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end to end: set Settings > Science > MPC observatory code = W88, then Analytics > Science > MPC Report Export > Select All > Export to File produced exports/mpc_report_2026-08-03T21-00-53-193015Z.txt. Columns extracted programmatically: each 80-char record has col 13 = ' ', col 14 = 'C', col 15 = ' ' (cols 1-5 blank, 6-12 'NS0001 ', 16-32 date, 33-44 RA, 45-56 Dec, 66-70 magnitude, 71 band, 78-80 'W88'). The MPC optical-observation format defines column 14 as Note 1 and column 15 as Note 2, and Note 2 carries the observation type ('C' = CCD). Location correct and the code is explicit: mpc_export_service.dart:181-185, assembled at :225.

title: Photometry CSV export writes local wall-clock timestamps with no timezone, silently shifting every measurement by the observer's UTC offset
what_happened: Science Data Export > Photometry Measurements > CSV wrote /home/scdouglas/Documents/Skotiq/exports/photometry_2026-08-02T11-18-30.csv. The first data row's Timestamp column reads '2026-08-01T05:00:00.000'. The DB row it came from has timestamp = 1785574800, which is 2026-08-01T09:00:00Z. The CSV is emitting local time (UTC-4 here) in ISO-8601 shape with no offset and no 'Z'.
expected: Photometry timestamps are the input to period analysis, AAVSO/AID submissions and any cross-observer comparison; they must be UTC (ideally JD or HJD as well) and must carry the offset. Any script that parses this file as ISO-8601 will place every point 4 hours off, and the error changes with the observer's timezone and with DST inside a single observing season.
repro: Analytics > Science > export/database icon > Photometry Measurements > CSV. Compare the Timestamp column with `select timestamp from photometry_measurements order by timestamp limit 1` (unix seconds).
evidence: CSV row: '5,148,target_primary,target,512.0,512.0,100000.0,-0.00612,120.0,0.008,false,2026-08-01T05:00:00.000'; sqlite: id 581 timestamp 1785574800 = 2026-08-01 09:00:00 UTC. The same file's own name is stamped '2026-08-02T11-18-30' (local) while the science report's footer uses Z - three conventions across the export surface.
where: the science CSV export writer used by ScienceExportHub (it calls toIso8601String() on a local DateTime rather than .toUtc())
proposed_fix: Emit `dt.toUtc().toIso8601String()` (which appends Z) and add a JD column; state the convention in the CSV header comment.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced and checked against the DB rather than another app readout. Science Data Export > Photometry Measurements > CSV wrote exports/photometry_2026-08-03T16-55-58.csv whose first data row's Timestamp column is '2026-08-01T05:00:00.000'; sqlite says that row's timestamp is 1785574800 = 2026-08-01 09:00:00 UTC, and the host is EDT (UTC-4). So the file emits local wall-clock in ISO-8601 shape with no offset and no Z. The claim's 'where' is vague; the precise location is science_export_hub.dart:1014, and the identical bug repeats for the other six CSV datasets at :1067, :1128, :1176, :1226, :1278, :1334, plus the filename stamp at :831. science_report_exporter.dart:99/111 uses .toUtc(), so the inconsistency the claim describes is real.

title: Transient Discovery Report: the AAVSO and MPC network chips are inert and the app never shows why, because the reason is only rendered for the already-selected network
what_happened: Analytics > Science > export icon > Transient Discovery Report > Open, with a confirmed detection selected ('AT 2026abc / New source / SNR 28.4 / confirmed'). The Network row offers AAVSO, MPC and TNS. TNS is pre-selected and shows a red explanation ('TNS submission needs your bot id/name, reporting group, data source, reporter, and api key'). Clicking AAVSO and clicking MPC does nothing - the selection stays on TNS and no message appears. I clicked each twice and re-read the tree after both.
expected: A user who cannot use TNS should be told, in the panel, why the other two networks are also unavailable. The app already computes exactly that text - _disabledReason() returns 'MPC astrometry is for moving objects - this detection is not a plausible mover' and an AAVSO-specific reason - but it is only rendered for _format, which the user cannot change to a disabled network. The explanation is written and permanently unreachable.
repro: Seed a transient_detections row with reviewed=1 and kind='newSource'; leave the TNS bot credentials and AAVSO observer code unset. Open the panel and click the AAVSO and MPC chips.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/ra3-49-tr2.png (TNS selected with its reason; AAVSO and MPC dim); accessibility tree after clicking AAVSO and after clicking MPC is byte-identical to before, still showing the TNS reason.
where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/analytics/widgets/transient_report_panel.dart:129-141 (chip onTap is null when !enabled) and :142-148 (the reason Text is guarded by `if (!_formatEnabled(_format, ...))`, i.e. only for the selected format); the per-format reasons live at :369-402
proposed_fix: Let the user select a disabled network (keep Preview/Submit disabled) so its reason renders, or render a one-line reason under every disabled chip.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with a seeded transient_detections row (reviewed=1, kind='newSource', SNR 28.4) and no credentials configured: the panel opens with TNS selected and its red reason shown; clicking the AAVSO chip and then the MPC chip left the accessibility tree byte-identical each time - selection stayed on TNS and no reason for either was ever rendered. Locations correct: transient_report_panel.dart:128-142 passes onTap: null when !enabled, :143-150 guards the reason Text on '!_formatEnabled(_format, ...)' i.e. only the selected format, and the per-format strings the user can never see live at :369-399.

title: Campaign Rollup contradicts itself three ways on one card: "Total integration 0.0h" beside "0.17h integration", and "No frames captured for this target yet" beside a session with 2 frames
what_happened: Analytics > Science > click the M13 campaign card. The Campaign Rollup dialog shows header tiles 'Sessions 1', 'Total integration 0.0h', 'Mean HFR 2.20', 'Effective imaging 0.0%'; then 'Per-filter progress: No frames captured for this target yet.'; then a Sessions list containing 'Night E - M13, Jul 31 2026 23:00 | - | 0.17h integration, HFR 2.20, RMS 0.60'. The session has 2 light frames of 300 s each = 0.167 h, which is exactly what the session row prints - and exactly what the total denies.
expected: One population per card. The header tiles and the per-filter breakdown count only accepted frames (both of this session's frames had just been rejected by the Image grader) while the per-session row counts all frames, so the dialog simultaneously asserts that the target has 0.0h and 0.17h of integration and that it has no frames and 2 frames. A user reading 'Total integration 0.0h / No frames captured for this target yet' for a target they imaged last night would conclude their data was lost.
repro: Give a target one session with N light frames. Analytics > Science > Grade N frames > reject them all. Open the target's campaign card.
evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/ra3-55-rollup.png; sqlite: session 5 has 2 light frames at exposure_duration 300.0 (0.167h) with is_accepted=0.
where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/campaign_rollup_service.dart (totalIntegration / per-filter aggregation filter on acceptance) vs the per-session row built from the session's own total_integration_secs in campaign_rollup_dialog.dart
proposed_fix: Aggregate the header, the per-filter table and the session rows from the same predicate, and label it ('accepted frames only'). If rejected frames are to be excluded, the session row must show '0.00h accepted (0.17h captured)'.
verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim. The M13 campaign card opens 'Campaign Rollup / M13' showing Sessions 1, Total integration 0.0h, Mean HFR 2.20, Mean seeing -, Effective imaging 0.0%, then 'Per-filter progress: No frames captured for this target yet.', then 'Night E - M13 / Jul 31, 2026 23:00 | - | 0.17h integration / HFR 2.20 / RMS 0.60'. Recomputed rather than compared: session 5 (target_id=4 = M13) has exactly 2 captured_images rows, both frame_type='light', exposure_duration 300.0, is_accepted=0, with imaging_sessions.total_integration_secs = 600.0; 600/3600 = 0.1667 -> the 0.17h row, and the accepted-light sum is 0.0 -> the 0.0h header. campaign_rollup_service.dart computes lightFrames as `frameType == 'light' && i.isAccepted`, feeding both totalCapturedIntegrationSecs (campaign_rollup_dialog.dart:172) and _buildFilters (empty -> the :226 'No frames captured' string), while the session row at campaign_rollup_dialog.dart:600 prints session.sessionIntegrationSecs. Both cited files are right. Correction for the fixer: the finding says 'the header tiles ... count only accepted frames', but only Total integration does - Mean HFR 2.20 and Effective imaging 0.0% come from the imaging_sessions rows with no acceptance filter, so the card mixes three populations, not two. Severity corrected DOWN to P2: each number is individually defensible (0.0h is the accepted integration; 0.17h is the captured integration), nothing downstream acts on it, and the defect is that one card labels different populations with the same words - sharpest in the flatly false 'No frames captured for this target yet.'
